title: On the (non-)existence of m-cycles for generalized Syracuse sequences
status: NOT CONSULTED: the publisher PDF at impan.pl loops on redirects, EuDML lists no alternate file, ResearchGate is blocked by policy; only the abstract, via EuDML and search snippets, was seen
notes: Acta Arithmetica 131 (2008), no. 3, 217-254. Registered 20 September 2026 during the search for a published 3x-1 verification floor. Per Lagarias's annotated bibliography II, entry 96, and the abstract: it generalizes the Simons-de Weger m-cycle non-existence proof to the 3x+q, px+1 and px+q problems, 'the inverse Collatz problem' -- which is 3x-1 -- generalized Collatz problems and the Roelants problem; a lower bound for the cycle length comes from a generalized lemma of Crandall, an upper bound for fixed m from Laurent-Rhin linear forms in logarithms. WHAT A READER SHOULD EXTRACT. Whether it states an m-cycle exclusion for 3x-1 over a range of m, and what verification floor for 3x-1 it assumes or cites to do so. If it does, that floor is the published number this laboratory searched for and did not find, and the m-cycle exclusion is the theorem-type statement the floor never gives. Unread here.
